items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5671

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the public health law, the social services law and
chapter 2 of the laws of 2004 amending the public health law, the
social services law and the state finance law relating to enacting the
assisted living reform act, in relation to reporting requirements by
the department of health; to repeal certain provisions of the public
health law and the social services law relating thereto; to repeal
section 10 of chapter 409 of the laws of 1991 relating to providing
for the submission of certain reports and written plans by certain
state departments, the omnibus economic development act of nineteen
hundred eighty-seven, and the New York state urban development
corporation act, relating to reporting requirements; to repeal section
2 of the families in transition act of 2000, relating to an annual
reporting requirement; and to repeal section 24-b of part B of chapter
58 of the laws of 2007 amending the elder law and other laws relating
to the elderly pharmaceutical insurance coverage program, program
eligibility and the generic drug dispensing fee, relating to reporting
requirements

 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

This bill would repeal or modify obsolete and outdated statutory
provisions that require the issuance of certain reports.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 would amend provisions related to the 21st Century Workgroup
for disease elimination to require a report every three years, rather
than annually.

Section 2 would repeal a requirement for the Department of Health
(DOH) to issue quarterly reports on the transfers or interchanges made
by the Commissioner related to state hospitals, including the
programmatic impact of each transfer or interchange.

Section 3 would repeal a requirement for DOH to report on the progress
of the immunization program.

Section 4 would repeal provisions related to the evaluation and
reporting of rape crisis intervention and prevention programs.

Section 5 would repeal provisions requiring the state health research
council to issue an annual report.

Section 6 would repeal provisions requiring the pesticide control
board to issue an annual report.

Section 7 would repeal provisions related to reporting on the
immunization of all students.

Section 8 would repeal provisions related to reporting on the
evaluation of the cancer registry.

Section 9 would amend provisions related to skin cancer reporting to
require a report every three years, rather than annually.

Section 10 would repeal a requirement to report on dioxin exposure
policies.

Section 11 would repeal provisions related to a special program on
diethylstilbestrol.


Section 12 would amend provisions related to child food choking
prevention to require a report every three years, rather than
annually.

Section 13 would repeal a requirement to report on the implementation
of the child health plus program.

Section 14 would; epeal a mandate to report on the effectiveness of
reaching the goals of the adolescent pregnancy prevention program.

Section 15 would repeal a report on the plans and activities of the
bureau of chronic disease and geriatrics.

Section 16 would repeal a requirement to report on findings, progress
and activities of the New York State Kidney Disease Institute.

Section 17 would repeal a requirement for the Public Health and Health
Planning Council (PHHPC) to report on uniform reports and accounting
systems for hospital costs.

Section 18 would repeal provisions mandating a report on rural health
networks.

Section 19 would repeal a requirement to report on the operation of
the multipayor patient centered medical home program.

Sections 20 through 22 would repeal several reports required of the
patient safety center.

Section 23 would repeal a report on the effectiveness of the Antonio
G. Olivieri controlled substances therapeutic research program.

Section 24 would repeal a report on the appropriateness of the
exclusion of hospital-based certified home health agencies and
allocations to publicly-sponsored certified home health agencies.

Section 25 would repeal a report on toxic substances.

Section 26 would repeal a report on the progress of implementation of
automated systems for Medicaid enrollment.

Section 27 would repeal a report on implementation of the AIDS home
care programs.

Section 28 would repeal status reports required of the AIDS Institute.

Section 29 repeal a mandate for DOH to submit an annual report
identifying services currently provided to children and adolescents
who lose their primary caregivers to HIV/AIDS.

Section 30 would repeal a reporting requirement pertaining to the
inactive Adult Care Facilities and Assisted Living Residences Task
Force.

Section 31 would repeal reports related to currently inactive child
health and wellness programs.

Section 32 would set for the effective dates.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :

The Public Health Law, Social Services Law, and Unconsolidated Law is
replete with DOH reporting requirements, many of which necessitate
reporting on an annual or biannual basis. However, many of these
reports are tied to programs that are obsolete or inactive.
Furthermore, many of the reporting requirements require DOH to report
on data that has already been made available to the public through
various data reporting systems. This bill will serve as a technical
clean up, eliminating obsolete reporting provisions in the law, and
will also amend select reporting requirements to change their
frequency to ensure the information provided in those reports is
provides a complete view of the program.

 POSSIBLE OBJECTIONS :

None.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 LOCAL IMPACT :

None.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The Public Health Law, Social Services Law, and Unconsolidated Law is

None.
